queries: Schrimpf 2021 neural architecture of language integrative modeling converges on predictive processing PMC

sources_considered.why: MIT repository record of a peer-reviewed PNAS paper whose authors say transformer language models give evidence about how human language comprehension works.

evidence_items.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (via MIT DSpace)

receipt.public_excerpt: These results provide computationally explicit evidence that predictive processing fundamentally shapes the language comprehension mechanisms in the human brain.

evidence_items.explanation: Before the post, peer-reviewed authors said transformer LMs gave evidence about the mechanisms of human language comprehension. That cuts against 'anything whatsoever' for the mind. Whether it explains 'why' in the speaker's sense is contested, so it is context, not decisive.

unresolved_gaps: No agreed standard exists for when a model-based finding counts as teaching us 'why the world is as it is rather than some other way'.
I did not review the full literature on LLMs in cognitive science or physical science before March 2023.
